the nuclear export signal of steroid hormone receptors does not mediate the nucleocytoplasmly shuttling of these receptors.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of nucleocytoplasmatic shuttling and nuclear export of steroid hormone receptors.
the molecular mechanisms of nuclear export of steroid receptors, in particular the progesterone receptor.
the mechanisms of nucleocytoplasmatic shuttling of the progesterone receptor, which is a member of the superfamily of steroid hormone receptors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nuclear export signal is not involved in the export of steroid receptors from the nucleus, and the nuclear export signal of steroid receptors is not a RanGTPase-dependent mechanism.
the nuclear export mechanism of steroid hormone receptors is different from the one described for most other nuclear proteins.
the export of PR does not depend on Ran GTP, but it depends on the NLS of PR.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PR export from nuclei is mediated by its NLS.
PR shuttles between the cytoplasm and nucleus in a GTP-independent manner and is dependent on the NLS.
PR is exported from nuclei by an NLS-dependent mechanism that is independent of the Ran guanosine triphotphate cycle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nucleocytoplasm shuttling of the progesterone receptor does not involve the nuclear export signal, but rather the nuclear localization signal.
